data.summary: This two‑week plan tackles the AP Chemistry exam by front‑loading the weak unit on Acids and Bases, integrating a live class, and then reviewing all units with timed practice. Each week is limited to 8 hours of focused study, with concrete tasks that can be completed in a single sitting.

weeks.focus: Master the fundamentals of acids, bases, and their equilibria while reinforcing key concepts from other units.
tasks: Do 15 practice problems on pH calculations for strong acids and bases, then check answers with the scoring guide.
Write a concise summary of the difference between ionic and covalent bonds using 1.1 and 4.5 concepts.
Create flashcards for key terms in 8.1-8.3 and review them for 30 minutes.
Solve 10 stoichiometry problems that involve acid-base reactions, marking each step.

weeks.focus: Consolidate all units and simulate exam conditions with timed practice.
tasks: Take a 60‑minute timed quiz covering 1.2-1.5 and 2.1-2.5, then review mistakes.
Perform a 30‑minute practice on the Ideal Gas Law (3.4) and kinetic theory (5.1).
Complete a 20‑minute worksheet on Gibbs Free Energy (9.3) and relate it to reaction spontaneity.
Do a 15‑minute review of equilibrium constants (7.1) using sample problems.

data.final_week_advice: Use the last week for a full-length practice exam under timed conditions, then spend the remaining time reviewing incorrect answers and reinforcing weak concepts.
